clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old girl born to consanguineous parents presented with a 10-year history of recurrent left migrainous headaches associated with intermittent ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy. At age 8, she developed left orbito-frontal throbbing headache with nausea, vomiting, and photophobia. Within 10 days, ptosis and left monocular horizontal diplopia appeared and persisted for 45 days. This episode of ophthalmoplegia relapsed three times at ages 13, 16, and 17, with spontaneous resolution after approximately one month each time. Concurrently, she developed increasingly frequent and disabling headaches occurring twice weekly without ophthalmoplegia. Brain MRI performed one year from the last attack revealed an enhancing nodule on the cisternal segment of the left oculomotor nerve, with imaging characteristics (location in cisternal segment and persistent nodular enhancement even during asymptomatic periods) highly suggestive of schwannoma. On follow-up, she no longer presented additional episodes.
